newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa attends Christmas mass.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa attends Christmas mass.

text.p: Mother Teresa, who returned home last week to continue recovering from heart surgery, led a Christmas mass at her Calcutta mission on Tuesday after earlier indications she might not appear publicly.
The mass was held at 8 p.m., four hours before a customary midnight mass, to enable the 86-year-old Roman Catholic nun to lead the 90-minute ceremony, aides said.
"Love one another as Jesus loves each one of you," the Nobel peace prize winner said in her message, delivered while seated.
Mother Teresa earlier watched a Nativity play staged by volunteers from all over the world at the courtyard of her mission and home.

Mother Teresa, known as the Saint of the Gutters for her devotion to the poor and dying, spent three weeks in hospital in August and September for heart trouble, malaria and pneumonia. Two weeks later, she fell off a chair and struck her head.
In November, she underwent an operation to unblock two coronary arteries for the third heart operation in five years.
She returned home last week after a long period of recovery delayed by bronchitis and irregular heartbeat.
